name: Reversing CNOT-conjugated rotations
summary: An X-rotation on the control and a Z-rotation on the target, between two CNOTs, can be moved to the other qubits by reversing the CNOTs.
description:
Conjugating $X(\beta)\otimes Z(\alpha)$ by a CNOT gives the commuting product of an $X\otimes X$ rotation by β and a $Z\otimes Z$ rotation by α. Conjugating $Z(\alpha)\otimes X(\beta)$ by the reversed CNOT gives the same two rotations, so the two circuits are equal.

In the ZX-calculus each side is a pair of phase gadgets (one of each colour) connecting the two qubits, which is why the identity holds.
